clues.fortune_text: After the 200 C zone the heat settles down: the next zone along is 120 C, golden and brown.
clues.nudge: Read past the rhyme. The couplet names two temperatures and which one comes later along the belt. The belt runs from zone 1 to zone 5.

clues.fortune_text: A newborn gnu calf trots at its mother's heels. 140 C follows 160 C just so, one zone after.
clues.nudge: The calf is a picture of following closely. The belt runs from zone 1 to zone 5, so after means further along the belt.

clues.fortune_text: Count the letters in vi's old rival from the editor wars. Set the zone with that number to 120 C.
clues.nudge: The editor wars are a decades-old friendly argument between fans of two text editors. One of them is vi: find the other and count its letters.

clues.fortune_text: The gnu wrote zone 1's heat in hex: 0xA0 degrees C.
clues.nudge: 0x marks a hexadecimal number. The first digit counts sixteens and the second counts ones; A means 10, B means 11, up to F for 15.

clues.fortune_text: assert zone[180] == zone[140] + 1  # zone 1 comes first, +1 is one zone after
clues.nudge: zone[t] means the number of the zone set to t degrees. An assert must be true, so read the line as plain arithmetic about two zone numbers.

clues.fortune_text: Thermostat pins: pin n reads zone n. The 200 C probe is wired one pin after the 180 C probe.
clues.nudge: Each temperature probe reads one zone and plugs into the matching pin, so pin numbers are zone numbers and neighbouring pins differ by one.
